pcto_intro_para1: Last year I had the chance to work alongside the team at SYEEW S.r.l., a young company building a SaaS business intelligence platform for micro and small enterprises. The goal? To make business numbers as clear as traffic lights: green when everything is smooth, red when action is needed.
pcto_intro_para2: Since the team was small, I got to work closely with everyone, learning about different priorities and making a hands-on contribution. There was no dedicated UX department, so I managed the process myself while regularly discussing ideas with the CEO and my technical tutor.
about_syeew_para1: Founded in 2020, SYEEW is an innovative start-up based in Jesi that aims to change how micro and small businesses read their data. Its mission is simple yet ambitious: make numbers instantly understandable through a visual interface that uses business emojis to show economic and operational trends.
about_syeew_para2: Behind the apparent simplicity lies sophisticated technology combining data integration, automation, and AI modules. The platform collects information from various sources, normalizes and processes it, then presents it clearly so even those without analytical skills can make informed decisions.
about_syeew_para3: In 2022 SYEEW received public funding of €100,000 covering 70% of a development project officially registered in the National Transparency Register. It's concrete recognition of the innovative value the company offers Italian SMEs.
modalita_main_title: Four ways to read your business
modalita_lead: SYEEW adapts to your schedule and needs through four modes designed for different levels of insight.
modalita_indaffarato_desc: This mode gives you a quick picture of your company's health without having to analyze anything. Four business emojis let you instantly read the overall situation: positive, negative, steady, or needs attention. It's a visual tool for those with little time who still want to stay in the loop.
modalita_curioso_desc: Curious lets you look a bit deeper, showing daily revenue details compared with a selected period. In just a few clicks you see how sales evolve day by day. It's light yet informative, great for keeping an eye on what's happening right now.
modalita_minuzioso_desc: This mode opens up a full analysis, item by item, with exact numbers and direct comparisons. Track key metrics like daily jobs, average price, revenue, and daily man-hours. SYEEW shows how close you are to reaching your goals, helping you fine-tune every aspect.
modalita_veggente_desc: With built-in artificial intelligence, this mode helps you plan with confidence by forecasting the coming months based on current and past data. You can set monthly targets and monitor progress. It's perfect for shifting from reactive management to a proactive approach.
emoji_section_lead: SYEEW turns complex company data into four straightforward emojis that instantly reveal how your business is doing. It's a gamified approach that makes analysis immediate, visual, and engaging.
emoji_scrigno_desc: Great job, the treasure's yours! Compared to the previous period, things are going very well. The Treasure Chest shows both your average sales price and operational efficiency have improved significantly. Your strategy is working—keep it up!
emoji_sirena_desc: The Mermaid keeps swimming even when the current is against her. You're on the right track, but something isn't quite perfect. Some indicators are positive, yet efficiency or average price may have dropped compared to before. It's time to dive deeper and see where to improve.
emoji_spia_desc: Nothing escapes the Spy's magnifying glass. It's here to alert you to hidden issues. Although efficiency or average price has risen, your overall performance has slipped. It might be time to revisit your strategy or investigate external factors.
emoji_sfinge_desc: Mysterious by nature, the Sphinx warns you with a deep red color that performance has worsened compared to the previous period. Not all is lost, but you need immediate action to steer back on course. Analyze the data, rethink your approach, and regain control.
tool_adobe_xd_desc: The starting point of the project. I analyzed the existing mockups created by the team to understand the initial interface structure and user flows. This helped identify what to keep and what to rethink during the redesign in Figma.
tool_figma_desc: The heart of the UX/UI design. I built a library of reusable components, defined a design system in line with SYEEW’s brand identity, and produced fully interactive prototypes. Real-time collaboration made gathering feedback and presenting designs to potential investors easy.
tool_flutter_dart_desc: Chosen for their ability to build native iOS and Android apps from a single code base. I implemented five main screens, translating the Figma designs into Dart code, managing smooth animations, page navigation, and mock data to simulate the final experience.
tool_vscode_desc: My main editor for Flutter development. Set up with the Dart and Flutter extensions for full language support, built-in debugging, and hot reload. It let me quickly test changes on a physical device via USB debugging.
experience_intro: When I arrived at SYEEW I was faced with a challenging yet stimulating situation: the company already had a mobile app developed years before in an outdated language. It was hard to maintain and couldn't keep up with modern UX expectations. They had an initial functional mockup in Adobe XD, but the design felt dated both aesthetically and in usability guidelines. My challenge was threefold: reinterpret that prototype by rebuilding it in Figma for more advanced components and auto-layout, update the style to a fresher visual identity consistent with the brand, and find the best technical path to convert the design into Flutter code for a cross-platform, scalable app.
experience_period1_para: During these three weeks I worked almost entirely in Figma, starting from the exported XD file. After attempts at automatic conversion recovered only about 40% of the layers, I chose to manually rebuild the interface. First I created a dedicated design system: color palette, hierarchical typography, icon styles, and a library of components like buttons, text fields, cards, dialogs, and snackbars. By the end, the file held over 20 components and 11 screens linked through prototypes simulating the main user flows—login, dashboard, viewing modes, profile, and settings. I shared the project with the team and external designers, using Figma’s in-app comments for feedback.
experience_period2_para_part1: Over these two weeks I translated the design into a well-organized, modular Flutter structure. All code lives under the main lib folder where I carefully separated pages, data models, and reusable components. Pages such as Login, ProfiloMaster, and the various sections (Busy, Curious, Meticulous, and Predictive) are under pages. Models for companies, ASAs, and profiles are in model, while common widgets live in a single file that includes elements like the bottom navigation bar, circular charts, summaries, and indicators.
experience_period2_para_part2: The main file, main.dart, loads demo data, sets the overall theme, and starts the app on the login screen. Users then reach their profile dashboard with a persistent bottom navigation bar giving access to four analysis modes. The most developed section is 'Busy,' which displays animated progress charts and circular summary bars for each ASA. Other sections are empty shells ready to expand.
experience_period2_para_part3: I used local JSON to mock data, allowing smooth interaction without real connections. Testing on a physical device in debug mode yielded over 58 frames per second and responsive performance. At the end I produced an APK along with build instructions for Flutter 3.22, letting the team test the app and consider future features like APIs or advanced login.
experience_period3_para1: On this day I joined SYEEW at SMAU Milan, one of Italy’s leading innovation fairs. We didn’t have a booth, but spent the day actively exploring, listening to pitches, and networking.
experience_period3_para2: I attended presentations and discussions that introduced me to many emerging realities; observing how different companies communicate their values, mission, and results was very instructive—some rely on data, others on emotional storytelling, still others on social impact.
experience_period3_para3: I jotted down notes and reflections that helped me grow as a worker and designer: I realized the importance of empathy in presenting a product and how design is a powerful tool in strategic communication.
experience_period3_para4: It was an intense and stimulating day, a chance to step outside the usual routine, get inspired, and return to work with a broader perspective.
review_para1: My time at SYEEW gave me a real taste of how a digital product comes to life, from blank page to working demo. I appreciated the trust and freedom to experiment. At the same time I felt the fast pace of a start-up: tasks like API integration or usability testing were left out due to timing.
review_para2: What struck me most was the CEO's total dedication: every detail, every screen, every strategy was handled with daily passion and care. It made me realize how rewarding it can be to build something from scratch and see it grow. It's an approach I hope to adopt for my own projects someday.
review_thanks_lead: I sincerely thank everyone on the team who made this experience possible. Thanks for the time, the precise suggestions, life advice, constant feedback, and every exchange of ideas.
review_thanks_para: This experience also helped me clarify my future: I discovered I want to continue studying Interaction Design. Working on the first assignment made me think more deeply about how people interact with digital interfaces, and it immediately fascinated me.
review_final_thanks: Thanks again for believing in me, for entrusting me with important challenges, and for providing the tools to face what comes next with confidence.
